title: TNOs found after May 2025 do not confirm or refute the 80-400 au Kuiper-belt warp; the result changes with the resonance screen, and exact tests give the original 46-object warp p = 0.035
abstract: Question: Siraj, Chyba and Tremaine (2025) found that the mean plane of 46 non-resonant trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs) at 80-400 au is about 15 degrees from the invariable plane (2.74 sigma, JPL SBDB of 2025-05-14). Do TNOs found later agree? Method: We reproduced their conditional von Mises likelihood from the 2026-11-12 SBDB, computed exact p-values by simulation with fixed object positions, and screened 25 new 80-400 au TNOs (first seen June 2025 to April 2026) for Neptune resonances with SBDynT. We compared the claimed warp plane and the invariable plane on the new objects with a likelihood ratio, calibrated by 4,000 conditional simulations per plane. Results: The reproduction gives 2.71 sigma (i0 = 13.3 deg, node 118 deg). The exact p-value is 0.035, and 0.082 for the three bins tested. Two high-inclination objects carry most of the signal. A two-component inclination model gives the same result. The new objects do not settle the question. With a strict screen (no resonant clone; 14 objects), they favour the warp (p = 0.018 against the invariable plane; combined 3.4 sigma). With the same best-fit screen for all objects (19 objects) or no screen (25), they favour the invariable plane (p = 0.039 and 0.017 against the warp; combined 2.1 sigma). Five 2025 objects with JPL covariances cause the difference: the strict screen removes them because some clones are resonant, while 2026 MPC-only orbits get only a best-fit check. Simulations show that about 100 new non-resonant objects give a 3-sigma test in either direction. Limitations: most new orbits have 62-133 day arcs, so their bins and resonance classes are uncertain; we used 30 clones, not 90; we did not rescreen the older objects or the 50-80 au bin. display.caption: Mean plane of non-resonant 80-400 au TNOs in (q0, p0) = sin(i0/2)(cos, sin) node0. Blue: the 46 objects of Siraj et al. (2025). Orange: TNOs found after May 2025 under three resonance screens (A strict, B best-fit, C none). Green: combined. Solid and dashed lines are the 68 % and 95 % likelihood regions; black X is the invariable plane. The new objects move the combined fit toward the warp under screen A and toward the invariable plane under screens B and C.

Forward test. Grey: simulated log-likelihood ratio Lambda (warp plane minus invariable plane) when the invariable plane is true; blue: when the Siraj et al. (2025) warp plane is true. Positions of the new objects are fixed. Orange line: observed value. Screen A favours the warp; screens B and C favour the invariable plane.

Per-object log-likelihood ratio (gamma = 15) against ecliptic longitude. Positive values favour the warp plane. Open squares: five 2025 objects with JPL covariances that the strict screen removes because some clones are resonant; they favour the invariable plane. Filled circles: 2026 MPC-only orbits that pass the strict screen.
